note: DRAFT written as a starting point - review and edit in the Author tool before the study. Enabled rules are inserted into every LLM prompt.

rules.text: The participant chose the direction (shorter, same steps, more detailed) and which elements to hide or show; these choices are final. You decide how far to go and which individual steps change, based on the data.
Use only runs of the current version that are not trial runs (is_trial false) to judge progress. Fewer than 2 such runs: be conservative.

For 'compress' from level 0 choose level 2 only if the participant is clearly fluent: the last two runs differ by less than about 15 % in total duration, have no back presses and no observer errors, and most steps are close to the reference (duration_vs_expected_ratio below about 1.5). Otherwise choose level 1.

Keep a step detailed (list it in keep_detailed_steps) when it shows struggle: observer errors, back presses, or a duration ratio above about 2 in the recent runs. Merging only the steps the participant masters is better than merging everything.
The participant's difficulty rating matters: 'hard' means be cautious (smaller step, keep more steps detailed); 'easy' supports a larger step.
For 'detail' go back one level unless the data shows clear struggle on the current version (several errors or back presses); then go back to level 0.

Condition gaze only: fluency shows as less looking at the instructions - falling dwell on text, image and video, more off_screen (looking at the bricks), fewer transitions and revisits. Many revisits to text or image mean a step is still hard. Ignore gaze for steps with very few valid samples.

Rewritten instruction texts are short imperative sentences in plain English that name the part, colour and target position. More compact versions use fewer words; detailed versions may add one helpful hint.
Choose media by their descriptions: for combined steps prefer the image that shows the target position; keep a method video only where the action is hard.
participant_message: English, friendly, simple, 1-3 short sentences, no numbers or technical terms. Describe what will be different and say they can try it and go back afterwards.
